main_issue: Who gets to use the living room window corner: D's twice-daily physio exercises vs A's desk, B's weekend guests, and C's laundry rack

A-B.evidence: A backs D's medical need over guests (T20) and seeks fixes for C's rack; B replies that the weekend problem remains unsolved (T21, T27).

A-C.evidence: A suggests wheeled rack and a plastic sheet (T24, T26); C rejects: 'It'll still drip everywhere' (T25), and C keeps refusing to move the rack.

A-D.evidence: A asks D's times and agrees to morning/evening (T7); D: 'Before 9 and after 6 is fine' (T8); A says 'He has a point' (T20).

B-C.evidence: Both defend their own use of the corner against D and neither addresses the other; they are aligned in resisting D's request (T15, T18, T21, T22).

B-D.evidence: D asks to work around friends' visits (T13, T16); B says it can't be planned (T15, T17, T21, T27).

C-D.evidence: D asks C to move the rack for 30 mins (T13); C: 'I can't just move the rack twice a day' (T18), 'It'll still drip' (T25).
